text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest merged PR first. It catches routing errors in real PRs without blocking merges, proving its value before we risk live traffic. The trade-off is delayed feedback for the newest open PR, but merged PRs are safer to test on and give clearer signals.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode on merged PRs only catches errors *after* they’re already in product—it’s a post-mortem, not prevention. Better to run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *open* PRs first: we catch routing errors before merges, and the trade-off is a cleaner signal than sifting through merged noise. Settle it by comparing error rates from shadow mode on open vs. merged PRs over one sprint.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest *open* PR first, then expand to merged PRs—this catches routing errors before they ship, proving value faster. Delaying merged PR tests avoids wasted shadow runs on already-fixed issues.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest open PR first. This catches routing errors before they merge, proving value faster and preventing bad changes from shipping. The trade-off is delayed feedback on merged PRs, but open PRs give clearer signals since they’re still active.

name: Ratchet
text:
DECISION: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest open PR first, then expand to merged PRs.

The result must deliver a working shadow-mode run on the newest open PR with clear routing-error signals, owned by Overhaul.
